## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `--exclude` flag does not read its default from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE`, which the project's CLI-flag policy requires, so it should be fixed before merge. The filtering logic and its tests had no other defects in this review.

## Changes
This pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` option. `collect()` uses it to skip files whose basename matches any of the patterns, and logs each skipped path. It also documents the flag in `docs/flags.md`, adds tests for parsing, filtering and the archive contents, and adds a one-line text fixture under `tests/fixtures/`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Read the --exclude default from ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE — Your new `--exclude` flag uses `default=[]` and never reads `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE`, so exclusions set in the environment are ignored. This breaks `.claude/skills/cli-flags/SKILL.md:11`: "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable … because CI sets options through the environment." — CI jobs that set exclusions through the environment will archive files they meant to skip, with no error. — Fix: Build the default from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` with a documented separator, update the `none` default in `docs/flags.md:7` to match, and extend `test_exclude_defaults_to_nothing` with an environment case.
